upsert.notes: Initial pilot study combining an oncolytic peptide with adoptive T-cell immunotherapy for previously untreated stage 3–5(a) canine B-cell lymphoma. upsert.title: Personalized mRNA-LNP immunotherapy for canine malignant tumors
upsert.center: PETcura (宝科雅) multicenter IIT
upsert.status: Recruiting — limited enrollment
upsert.contacts: WeChat: petcura; project team matches eligible owners with a participating veterinarian/hospital.
upsert.notes: Official study page updated 2026-08-15. Exploratory multicenter IIT for canine malignant tumors using fresh tumor plus paired adjacent normal tissue for >=50G RNA sequencing, neoantigen selection and personalized mRNA-LNP immunotherapy. T-cell lymphoma and brain tumors are explicitly excluded and therefore are not mapped to this record. Requires histologic or cytologic confirmation, age >=2 years, generally weight >=5 kg (smaller dogs may be individually assessed), fresh tumor and paired normal tissue obtainable at surgery; dogs already operated may still be considered if tissue was correctly frozen. Also requires adequate performance status/labs and successful LNP tolerance testing. Excludes recent chemotherapy/radiation/high-dose corticosteroids within 2 weeks, severe infection/autoimmune disease/immunodeficiency, pregnancy/lactation, and expected survival <6 months. Owners pay some sampling/freezing/sequencing costs; personalized mRNA design/manufacture is funded by PETcura.

upsert.title: Cryotherapy or intratumoral immunotherapy before amputation for canine osteosarcoma
upsert.center: Johns Hopkins Center for Image-Guided Animal Therapy (CIGAT)
upsert.status: Open and recruiting — listed on the current Johns Hopkins CIGAT clinical-trials page
upsert.contacts: Johns Hopkins CIGAT — 410-502-7325; contact through the official clinical-trials page
upsert.funding: Study covers PET-CT/CT imaging, cryotherapy or intratumoral immunotherapy, study-related medications, and follow-up imaging/blood tests. Required amputation and chemotherapy are not covered by the study.
upsert.notes: Treatment trial for histopathologically confirmed canine osteosarcoma. Eligible dogs receive PET-CT and either cryotherapy or two doses of tumor-injected immunotherapy before required amputation at about two weeks, followed by chemotherapy. Johns Hopkins lists no prior osteosarcoma treatment or chemotherapy for other cancers and requires the dog to be systemically healthy apart from osteosarcoma.

upsert.title: Radiation therapy plus temozolomide for canine brain tumors

upsert.contacts: Johns Hopkins CIGAT — 410-502-7325; contact through the official clinical-trials page
upsert.funding: Radiation therapy and chemotherapy are fully funded. Study-related medications for side effects, follow-up MRI, and blood tests are also covered; treatment after progression is not covered.
upsert.notes: Treatment study for dogs with a suspected glioma/intra-axial brain tumor greater than 1 cm on MRI and restricted to one side of the brain. Protocol uses five consecutive workdays of radiation therapy with concurrent oral temozolomide. Previous or current oncologic treatment of the brain tumor is exclusionary; investigator prescreening is required.

upsert.title: Vaxleukin-15 (recombinant canine IL-15) for canine mammary tumors

upsert.status: Approved and commercially available in South Korea
upsert.notes: Vaxleukin-15 (recombinant canine IL-15) is an approved veterinary immunoadjuvant treatment in South Korea. For canine mammary tumors, the approved use is in combination with surgical standard-of-care treatment, not as a replacement for surgery. The mammary-tumor indication was approved in 2024. Current 2026 company materials state that the product is being sold in South Korea through Yuhan. This is treatment access, not an actively recruiting clinical trial.

upsert.title: Vaxleukin-15 (recombinant canine IL-15) for canine lymphoma

upsert.status: Approved and commercially available in South Korea

Final prescribing/eligibility decisions are made by the treating veterinarian.

upsert.title: Experimental silver nanoparticle treatment for canine and feline cancer
upsert.center: Hospital Veterinario Peña Jasso / UNAM-UABC-UAG translational nanomedicine project
upsert.status: Recruiting — experimental treatment program
upsert.contacts: Enrollment is through Hospital Veterinario Peña Jasso in Ensenada, Baja California. Owners first register and the hospital performs a clinical evaluation to determine suitability for the experimental phase.
upsert.notes: Current 2026 translational program CBF-2025-G-82 led by Dr. Nina Bogdanchikova. A fresh recruitment report quotes the project veterinary collaborator directly: dogs and cats with a cancer diagnosis may be considered after individualized clinical review; 16 veterinary patients had already been treated at the time of reporting. Owners pay for pre-enrollment evaluation tests; once admitted, consultations, radiographs and follow-up studies are covered by the program. The experimental formulation uses PVP-stabilized silver nanoparticles developed through UNAM-associated research. UNAM's official academic/patent database independently confirms the underlying silver-nanoparticle anticancer composition and inventor team. Evidence of current veterinary recruitment is a direct investigator/collaborator statement in a 2026 news report rather than a dedicated institutional trial registry page, so final eligibility and continued enrollment must be confirmed with the hospital. Do not describe efficacy as established; this remains experimental translational treatment.

upsert.title: IL-15 immunotherapy for canine melanoma or osteosarcoma with pulmonary metastasis
upsert.center: Evergreen Animal Hospital (長青動物醫院), Taipei
upsert.status: Recruiting
upsert.contacts: Evergreen Animal Hospital main hospital oncology clinic, Taipei; phone 02-23369908. Ask for IL15臨床試驗.
upsert.notes: Official hospital recruitment page. Cytology- or histopathology-confirmed melanoma or osteosarcoma; breed, age, weight and sex unrestricted. Requires pulmonary metastatic lesion >1.0 cm and no life-threatening tumor-related symptoms. Current steroids or other immunosuppressants are not allowed. Owner must attend weekly treatment/follow-up for about 10-12 weeks. IL-15 is given weekly for 8 treatments, by subcutaneous injection and, for pulmonary metastatic disease, also via nebulized inhalation. IL-15 drug is free; diagnostics and supportive medications are owner-paid. IMPORTANT matcher prescreen: official protocol specifically requires a lung metastatic lesion >1.0 cm; current schema cannot encode the 1-cm pulmonary-lesion threshold separately, so final eligibility must confirm this criterion.

upsert.notes: Official sponsor recruitment notice dated 2025-10-26 remains publicly listed; sponsor subsequently announced regulatory approval to conduct the Taiwan field trial on 2025-11-03 and continues to describe PT001 as an active oncology development program in 2026. Multicenter randomized open-label two-arm field trial of PT001, a PD-L1 and CTLA-4 recombinant-protein therapeutic vaccine, for confirmed stage II-III canine oral malignant melanoma. Age >=1 year.
